newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: China invites top UN rights envoy, date to be set.
newsitem.headline: China invites top UN rights envoy, date to be set.

text.p: Jose Ayala Lasso, U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights, has accepted a government invitation to visit China, a U.N. spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
No date has been set for the trip, whose object would be to continue the "constructive dialogue" with Beijing on the human rights situation in China, according to Therese Gastaut.
"The dates and programme are being discussed," Gastaut told a news briefing in Geneva. "The timing has not yet been decided. It will certainly be this year, in the months to come," she added.

U.N. sources said they did not expect his mission to take place before the start of the U.N. Human Rights Commission's annual session in Geneva on March 10. Ayala Lasso is making his fifth trip to Rwanda next week.
In its annual report two weeks ago, the U.S. State Department accused China of effectively silencing all public dissent against the communist party and government last year.
The U.S. delegation is widely expected to co-sponsor a resolution on China at the 53-member forum.

Beijing last year successfully quashed a U.N. resolution critical of its human rights record which expressed concern over continued reports of violations of fundamental freedoms. It was the sixth year in a row that China managed to avert censure.
Ayala Lasso, named to the new post three years ago, attended the women's rights conference in Beijing in September 1995.
The only U.N. special rapporteur (investigator) to gain entry to China was Abdel-Fattah Amor, a Tunisian lawyer who went in November 1994 to look into religious intolerance.
In a report to the U.N. Commission on Human Rights the following month, he recommended that the constitution be amended to provide guarantees on freedom of religion.
